dataset_family: ADNI (ADNI-1, ADNI-GO, ADNI-2 FDG-PET; 168 MCI-c / 187 MCI-nc, 3-year window; 321 train/validation, 34 independent test)
method_family: 2D CNN (ZF-Net) deep-radiomics features from FDG-PET, concatenated with clinical variables (demographics, MMSE, MoCA, CDR-SB, APOE4), then a linear SVM (feature-level fusion)

what_it_shows: A single-study head-to-head on the same independent test group. PET deep-radiomics plus clinical variables (DLR+C) reached AUC 0.90, accuracy 90.62%. The comparators were clinical-only (AUC 0.81, 81.09%), SUVR+clinical (0.85, 85.35%), SUVR-only (0.68, 68.38%), ROI radiomics (73.31%, no AUC) and the ZF-Net imaging model alone (0.756, 74.12%). Adding clinical data to SUVR raised the AUC from 0.68 to 0.85.
why: STATED: yes. The study fuses PET imaging features with auxiliary clinical metadata and runs the comparison itself. The fused model beats every unimodal baseline the study ran, including a multivariable clinical-only model, the strongest non-imaging baseline (AUC 0.90 vs 0.81). NARROWED: yes. Adding clinical information to an imaging model improved on the same imaging model alone, both for the ZF-Net encoder (AUC 0.756 to 0.90) and for SUVR (AUC 0.68 to 0.85, both SVM on the same test group). CAVEATS: (1) No significance test between models is reported. The discussion claims 'significant superiority', but the only test compares decision scores between MCI-c and MCI-nc (p.6). (2) The independent test group is small: 16 MCI-c plus 18 MCI-nc (p.3), although the Table 1 header says n = 48. (3) The ZF-Net-alone figures use the CNN's own classifier, not an SVM on DLR features alone, so the imaging-only and fused pipelines are not identical. The SUVR vs SUVR+clinical pair is the cleaner like-for-like comparison. (4) The text puts the Table 2 ZF-Net figures on the independent test group, but the Table 2 footnote says 10-fold cross-validation. (5) Circularity: the clinical block includes CDR-SB and MMSE, which partly define conversion. (6) MCI-c scans were 'not all collected at the baseline' (p.3), which may favour the imaging signal for converters. INDEPENDENCE: ADNI, so no new dataset family. The method family (CNN on FDG-PET fused with cognitive scores) is close to P-81's, although P-190 extracts CNN features and fuses them in an SVM while P-81 concatenates inside an end-to-end 3D CNN.

quotes.quote: Among five methods, the DLR+C method showed the best performance with accuracy of 90.62 ± 1.16%, sensibility of 87.50 ± 0.00%, and specificity of 93.39 ± 2.19% in the independent test group. The performance of the SUVR method, radiomics method, clinical method, and SUVR+Clinical method were all poorer than our proposed method, with accuracies of 68.38 ± 1.27, 73.31 ± 6.93, 81.09 ± 1.97, and 85.35 ± 0.72% in the independent test group, respectively.

The average AUCs (±SD) of SUVR method, Clinical method, SUVR+Clinical method, and DLR+C method were 0.68 ± 0.01, 0.81 ± 0.02, 0.85 ± 0.01, and 0.90 ± 0.01, respectively, in the independent test group.
